pr.title: Keep short K writes row-major; enable VNNI K in the deb preset
Keep short K writes row-major; enable VNNI K in the deb preset
pr.head: 175b1837b9

short_version: PR #4901 is the last of the four PRs that split PR 4424: a 16-token block of K rows stays row-major inside its own 4 KiB until its 16th row is saved, the block is converted to the VNNI layout at the forward end, a block that decode completes under hardware attention stays row-major, and the deb preset turns the TRON_K_VNNI option on.

The page introduces three data models (the row-major tail block, the page's saved-row and converted-block bits, the storage reference k_storage_ref) and four mechanisms (the in-place conversion, the row recording with the deferred conversion list, the accessors and the clear and copy paths that follow the block bit, and the hardware-attention policy with the dense gate).

kv_cache-b2, kv_cache-b4, kv_cache-b1 and k_vnni-b4 carry the data models and the conversion, model-b5, kv_cache-b5, kv_cache-b3, k_vnni-b5 and k_vnni-b3 carry the protocols and the policy, and the seven other diagrams give the context that PR #4868 and PR #4898 built.

words.definition: Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. The kernel qk_vnni_128x4 reads a page's VNNI plane in place as its B operand (the second matrix of one tile multiply).
Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. The reader k_vnni::qk_group and the row-major dotter are AVX-512 code.
The 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K values. One 128-dimension K row is 128 bf16 = 256 bytes.
Page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15 of a plane, 4 KiB. A 64-token page has 4 blocks (c = 0..3).
One bit per block and storage slot, kept in the page. It is set when the block holds the VNNI layout. Every reader and writer of a row takes the row's layout from it.
64 bytes, the unit the CPU moves between memory and its caches. A row-major row is 4 whole lines. A VNNI column is 4 bytes in each of 64 lines.

The in-place rewrite of one block between its row-major form and its VNNI form, in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp. page::k_block_to_vnni_at runs block_to_vnni for every KV head of a storage slot and then sets the block bit.
A preset is a named CMake build configuration. The deb preset builds the released Debian package. This PR sets the option TRON_K_VNNI on in it, next to TRON_AMX_DISPATCH.
Prefill is prompt processing (many tokens per user per pass). Decode is one generated token per user per step.

A dense page is a full 64-token page that the query sees whole. The dense gate k_layout_dense in self_attention.hpp lets the kernel score a page only when every block of the page is converted (page::k_vnni_blocks equals BLOCKS_PER_PAGE_MASK_0XF, all 4 bits).

The per-token dot product of the main branch over one row-major row (struct dotter in h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp). From this PR it also scores the rows of a row-major block through their typed row row_major_row.

The separate K/V storage view of EAGLE speculative decoding (a draft-model technique). While it is selected, logical slot 0 addresses the extra physical slot and the extra K layout state entry (index layout_t::n_slots).
The point of a pass after the plugin's run() joined its workers and the cooperative staging drained (wait_for_coop_gof). convert_pending_k_blocks converts the blocks the pass completed there.
Field-programmable gate array, the card that scores hardware attention.

A GOF is a group of four consecutive tokens. The staging (gof::populate) copies their K and V rows into a buffer that DMA (direct memory access) moves to the FPGA card. Cooperative staging is that work done by idle attention workers (help_drain_gof) and by the main thread (wait_for_coop_gof).
Attention scored by the FPGA over the K/V it holds. cached_operation_uses_hw(operation) says, once per model, whether an operation's K is scored there.

Issue #4500 records the FPGA-attention decode loss of the per-token 64-line column (qwen3-4b: 2.2 % at tp2 and 9.7 % at tp4). Issue #4934 tracks the decode slowdown of this PR against its parent with the kill switch.

k_storage_ref pairs a physical storage slot with the index of its K layout state. k_state_ix maps logical slot 0 to the EAGLE entry while the EAGLE view is active, and to the slot's own index otherwise.
The AMX routine of PR #4887 that scores one dense page from the VNNI-packed plane, with the query pack as its A operand.
TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 stops the AMX kernels at run time. The layout stays, and the reader scores the VNNI blocks.
One key/value head. kv_mul is the number of query heads that share one KV head (the query group).
A 64-token unit of the KV cache. The page struct keeps the per-token save counters and, from this PR, the two K layout bit sets.
One transformer layer. In the uniform topology the cache has one logical slot per layer.
Helper threads of the main thread in the generated plugins (worker_ix 1 .. n_workers - 1). PR #4898 lets them share the K store window.
The thread that runs the serial part of a forward pass (worker 0 of a generated plugin). Only it records row bits and converts blocks.
One chunk of a pass's token jobs that the forward runs together. A block may be split across two minibatches of one pass.
A CMake option that selects VNNI-packed K storage for every 128-dimension head through the gate k_vnni::layout_on. It is off in every preset except, with this PR, the deb preset.
The std::vector of {page, k_storage_ref, block} entries that save_k fills on the main thread, one per row that completes an unconverted block. convert_pending_k_blocks drains it at the forward end.

A plane is K for one KV head of one page (64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB). A panel is 1 KiB for one 32-dimension step and one 16-token block. A pair row is one 64-byte line that holds one dimension pair for 16 tokens.
A pull request of the tron repository. The stack is PR #4868, #4887, #4898 and #4901, each based on the one before.
The prompt length of a benchmark cell, passed as runtron --prompt-length. Every run then generates 256 tokens.

The AVX-512 routine of PR #4868 that scores a query group against the converted blocks of a page, one token per vector lane. From this PR it scores only the tokens whose live bit is set, and a row-major block keeps its bits clear.
One contiguous row of 128 bf16 per token. Every head size other than 128 keeps this layout, and a row-major block inside a VNNI plane holds its rows this way.
A 16-token block of a VNNI plane whose rows are stored row-major until all 16 rows are saved. Token t of block c owns 256 contiguous bytes at row_major_row, in panel (t / 4, c), row t % 4.
One bit per page offset and storage slot, kept in the page, set when the K row at that offset is saved. note_k_row_saved sets one bit, and note_k_block_saved sets the 16 bits of a block at once.
The physical storage of one persistent K/V storage region (kv_storage_offset). A logical slot (kv_slot_id) maps to one under the active view.
Tokens per second, the decode throughput measure of the PR body's Performance section.
The lock on the scheduler's token tree. Clears (clear_kv_complete_at) and page copies (copy_from) run between forward passes with it held, so no forward pass reads the book meanwhile.
The inference program under test. runtron is its command-line tool.

Vector Neural Network Instructions layout: the two values of one dimension pair of a token sit side by side, and one 64-byte row holds that pair for 16 consecutive tokens. It is the B-operand layout of the AMX tile multiply. VNNI-packed is the storage sense of packed.

The store of a run of 16 tokens that fills one block, written directly in the VNNI layout (PR #4898). This PR drops its mask parameter and makes the caller publish the block's bits with note_k_block_saved.
The shared K store of one minibatch (PR #4898). The main thread cuts the items into work units (runs inside one block of one page), opens the window, and the main helpers claim units.

what_lands.concept: Forgetting rows and page copies carry the bits
what_lands.where: h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2474-2478 (clear_kv_complete_at calls k_forget_row), 2549-2591 (k_forget_row), 2693-2788 (copy_storage_slot with k_storage_ref and the bit arithmetic), 2792-2808 (copy_from builds the pair)
what_lands.note: When a new token takes a page offset, the bits at and above it are dropped in every storage slot, and a converted block that keeps live rows below the offset goes back to row-major first. A page copy makes the touched destination blocks row-major, copies row by row, and converts the blocks that are complete afterwards.

what_lands.concept: The hardware-attention policy

what_lands.note: When the FPGA scores an operation's K, save_k records no row bits for the rows a short run stores and queues no block, so a block that decode completes stays row-major. Whole-block saves still store the VNNI layout and set their bits.

what_lands.concept: The dense gate and the dotter for tail rows

walkthrough.say: This is the last PR of the stack, and it answers issue #4500: a generated token's K row written across 64 cache lines cost 2.2 % to 9.7 % of FPGA-attention decode throughput. The fix keeps an incomplete 16-token block row-major in its own bytes, converts it once at the forward end, and never converts the blocks that decode completes under hardware attention. Open the PR body's Short version and the stack table at the end of it.

Point at the two drawings of block 2: the same 4 KiB holds either four 256-byte rows per panel (the row-major form, row_major_row) or the 16 pair rows per panel (the VNNI form). Point at store_row_major / load_row_major, then at block_to_vnni and block_to_rows, and at the block bit k_vnni_blocks_ that says which form the block holds. Open h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:445-502 for the Note and the three row-major operations.

Walk the states left to right: empty, incomplete (row-major), complete and waiting, converted. The 16th row sets the last row bit (note_k_row_saved, kv_cache.hpp:2169-2185), the forward end converts (k_block_to_vnni_at, 2216-2238), and the arc over the top is the whole-block save that goes straight to converted (note_k_block_saved, 2194-2202). Then point at the lower path: under hardware attention save_k records no bits, so the block never converts (model.hpp:3420-3425).

Point at the page column: k_rows_saved_ (one 64-bit word per state entry) and k_vnni_blocks_ (one byte per state entry), with one entry per logical slot plus the EAGLE entry. Point at k_state_ix and k_storage_ref: a logical slot maps to a state entry and a physical storage slot under the current view, and the pending list keeps the resolved pair. Open h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2613-2627 and 2139-2157.

Follow the bytes of block 2: store_row_major writes 4 whole lines per token, block_to_vnni rewrites all 64 lines once at the forward end, store_row and load_row then touch 4 bytes in every one of the 64 lines for one token, and block_to_rows puts the row-major form back. Say the cost argument out loud: 4 lines per token in the row-major form against 64 in the VNNI form, for the store, the dotter and the FPGA staging gather. Open h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:503-533 for the two conversions and their 4 KiB stack copy.

Point at the run test: a run of 16 takes set_k_block and note_k_block_saved, any shorter run takes set_k_row per token (model.hpp:3303-3339), and set_k_row picks store_row_major or store_row from the block bit (kv_cache.hpp:2255-2260). Then point at the recording loop after the join (model.hpp:3419-3437): one note_k_row_saved per KV token, a push onto pending_k_blocks_ when a row completes an unconverted block, and the whole loop skipped when cached_operation_uses_hw is true. Point at convert_pending_k_blocks at the bottom (3176-3183).

Point at the tinted band: the cooperative GOF staging gather of an earlier minibatch can still read a block's rows row-major while a later minibatch of the same pass saves the block's last rows, so the conversion waits until after wait_for_coop_gof. Open h/tron/models/model.hpp:1836-1847 to show run(), wait_for_coop_gof and convert_pending_k_blocks in that order. Then point at the token tree lane: clear_kv_complete_at and copy_from run between passes under the tree lock, so k_forget_row and copy_storage_slot need no bit synchronisation beyond it.

Use the rows as a checklist of every reader and writer: set_k_row / get_k_row branch on the block bit, k_row_if_row_major hands the FPGA staging a row-major row in place (full.hpp:2762-2764), k_forget_row drops bits and converts back (kv_cache.hpp:2557-2591), and copy_storage_slot carries the bits with the rows (2693-2788). Point at the apply_page_tok row: the dense gate k_layout_dense admits the kernel only when all four block bits are set, otherwise qk_group scores the converted blocks and the dotter scores the tail rows (self_attention.hpp:1924-1935, 2019-2033). Point at the dashed band of private helpers, all new.

Read the thread rules R1 to R7: any thread of the window stores rows and publishes whole-block bits, only main records row bits after the join, only main converts at the forward end, the attention workers and the staging only read, and the scheduler thread converts back under the tree lock. R7 is the hardware-attention exception. Open h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:729-764 for the Note that states the policy and its accepted cost (a score can differ by fp32 add order alone when software scores such a block).

Show the three new groups of the function model: the bit helpers block_bit / offset_bit, the row-major form (row_major_row, store_row_major, load_row_major) and the conversion (block_to_vnni, block_to_rows). The grey caller boxes at the left name where each is used, and every other cell is PR-1 or PR-3 content Ben has seen already.

Point at the forward-end lane: convert_pending_k_blocks sits on main's serial path after wait_for_coop_gof. Its cost, 4 KiB of plane data per block and KV head, is not measured at this head, which is the open item the PR body names with the convert_k_blocks trace span. The hardware-attention policy avoids that cost for the blocks the kernel never reads.

Close with the build and the evidence: CMakePresets.json:68-69 turns the option on in the deb preset, and README.ci.md:591-597 says the layout does not depend on AMX. Name the three mutation checks of the PR body and the FPGA cells: +2.5 % and +12.1 % decode TPS against the parent at prompt 1,024 tokens, inside the band against main. Then the two reviewer decisions: never converting under hardware attention, and shipping the option on in the package.

pr.title: Keep short K writes row-major; enable VNNI K in the deb preset
pr.head: 175b1837b9

short_version: PR #4901 is the last of the four PRs that split PR 4424: a 16-token block of K rows (saved key vectors) stays row-major (one contiguous row per token) in its own 4 KiB until its 16th row is saved, and the block is converted to the VNNI layout (the value order the AMX kernel reads) at the end of that forward pass.

Under hardware attention (attention scored on the FPGA card) a block that decode completes stays row-major, and the deb preset (the build configuration of the released package) turns the layout option TRON_K_VNNI on.

The page introduces the PR's three data models (the row-major tail block, the page's saved-row and converted-block bits, the storage reference) and four mechanisms (the in-place conversion, the row recording with its deferred conversion list, the accessors and the clear and copy paths that follow the block bit, the hardware-attention policy with the dense gate) on nine core diagrams (kv_cache-b2, kv_cache-b1, kv_cache-b4, k_vnni-b4, model-b5, kv_cache-b5, kv_cache-b3, k_vnni-b5, k_vnni-b3), and seven context diagrams carry what PR #4868, #4887 and #4898 built.

words.definition: Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. The kernel qk_vnni_128x4 reads a page's VNNI plane in place as its B operand (the second matrix of one tile multiply).
The pool threads that run the attention kernels of a layer. They read a pending page only after every minibatch that writes it counted its latch (upstream_kvs_ready, a countdown) down.
Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. The reader k_vnni::qk_group and the row-major dotter are AVX-512 code.

The noise band of the PR body's Performance section: twice the larger of the two binaries' sample standard deviations over 3 repetitions, never smaller than 0.4 TPS or 0.15 s. A difference beyond it counts as a change.
The 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K values. One 128-dimension K row is 128 bf16 = 256 bytes.
Page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15 of a plane, 4 KiB. A 64-token page has 4 blocks (c = 0..3).
One bit per block and storage slot, kept in the page. It is set when the block holds the VNNI layout. Every reader and writer of a row takes the row's layout from it.
The struct that owns one KV cache allocation (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:942). A page is a lightweight reference into it.
64 bytes, the unit the CPU moves between memory and its caches. A row-major row is 4 whole lines. A VNNI column is 4 bytes in each of 64 lines.

The in-place rewrite of one block between its row-major form and its VNNI form, in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp. page::k_block_to_vnni_at runs block_to_vnni for every KV head of a storage slot and then sets the block bit.

A preset is a named CMake build configuration. The deb preset builds the released Debian package. This PR sets the option TRON_K_VNNI on in it, next to TRON_AMX_DISPATCH (AMX dispatch, the CMake option that compiles the AMX kernels).
Prefill is prompt processing (many tokens per user per pass). Decode is one generated token per user per step.

A dense page is a full 64-token page that the query sees whole. The dense gate k_layout_dense in self_attention.hpp lets the kernel score a page only when every block of the page is converted (page::k_vnni_blocks equals BLOCKS_PER_PAGE_MASK_0XF, all 4 bits).

The per-token dot product of the main branch over one row-major row (struct dotter in h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp). From this PR it also scores the rows of a row-major block through their typed row row_major_row.

The separate K/V storage view of EAGLE speculative decoding (a draft-model technique). While it is selected, logical slot 0 addresses the extra physical slot and the extra K layout state entry (index layout_t::n_slots).
The point of a pass after the plugin's run() joined its workers and the cooperative staging drained (wait_for_coop_gof). convert_pending_k_blocks converts the blocks the pass completed there.
The 32-bit float format in which the score kernels add. The row-major dotter and the reader add in a different order.
Field-programmable gate array, the card that scores hardware attention.

A GOF is a group of four consecutive tokens. The staging (gof::populate) copies their K and V rows into a buffer that DMA (direct memory access) moves to the FPGA card. Cooperative staging is that work done by idle attention workers (help_drain_gof) and by the main thread (wait_for_coop_gof).
Attention scored by the FPGA over the K/V it holds. cached_operation_uses_hw(operation) says, once per model, whether an operation's K is scored there.

Issue #4500 records the FPGA-attention decode loss of the per-token 64-line column for the model qwen3-4b: 2.2 % at tp2 and 9.7 % at tp4 (tp2, tp4: the model split over 2 or 4 shards, tensor parallelism). Issue #4934 tracks the decode slowdown of this PR against its parent with the kill switch.

k_storage_ref pairs a physical storage slot with the index of its K layout state. k_state_ix maps logical slot 0 to the EAGLE entry while the EAGLE view is active, and to the slot's own index otherwise.
The AMX routine of PR #4887 that scores one dense page from the VNNI-packed plane, with the query pack as its A operand (the first matrix of the tile multiply).
TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 stops the AMX kernels at run time. The layout stays, and the reader scores the VNNI blocks.
One key/value head. kv_mul is the number of query heads that share one KV head (the query group).
A 64-token unit of the KV cache. The page struct keeps the per-token save counters and, from this PR, the two K layout bit sets.
One transformer layer. In the uniform topology (every slot shares one geometry, one logical slot per layer) the cache has one logical slot per layer.
The main branch of the tron repository, the base of PR #4868. In the labels of this page, 'from: main' means the code existed before the stack.
Helper threads of the main thread in the generated plugins (worker_ix 1 .. n_workers - 1). PR #4898 lets them share the K store window.

The thread that runs the serial part of a forward pass (worker 0 of a generated plugin). Only it records the row bits of the runs shorter than a block (note_k_row_saved, after the join) and converts the queued blocks at the forward end. A whole-block save publishes its 16 row bits and its block bit from any thread of the window (note_k_block_saved).
One chunk of a pass's token jobs that the forward runs together. A block may be split across two minibatches of one pass.
A deliberate code change that the named test must fail on. The PR body reports three.
A named comment block in the tron source. Other comments refer to it by this name.
A CMake option that selects VNNI-packed K storage for every 128-dimension head through the gate k_vnni::layout_on. It is off in every preset except, with this PR, the deb preset.
PR #4898, the base of this PR. The PR body's Performance section compares against it under the name head.
One forward() call that runs every layer for one step's tokens. The forward end is its last part on the main thread.
The std::vector of {page, k_storage_ref, block} entries that save_k fills on the main thread, one per row that completes an unconverted block. convert_pending_k_blocks drains it at the forward end.

A plane is K for one KV head of one page (64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB). A panel is 1 KiB for one 32-dimension step and one 16-token block. A pair row is one 64-byte line that holds one dimension pair for 16 tokens.
A pull request of the tron repository. The stack is PR #4868, #4887, #4898 and #4901, each based on the one before.
The prompt length of a benchmark cell, passed as runtron --prompt-length. Every run then generates 256 tokens.

The AVX-512 routine of PR #4868 that scores a query group against the tokens of a page whose bit is set in its live mask (a 64-bit mask, one bit per page offset), one token per vector lane. From this PR the caller must keep the bits of a row-major block clear and score those tokens with the dotter, so every block with a live bit holds the VNNI layout (h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:43-46).
One contiguous row of 128 bf16 per token. Every head size other than 128 keeps this layout, and a row-major block inside a VNNI plane holds its rows this way.
A 16-token block of a VNNI plane whose rows are stored row-major until all 16 rows are saved. Token t of block c owns 256 contiguous bytes at row_major_row, in panel (t / 4, c), row t % 4.

save_k (two overloads in h/tron/models/model.hpp:3465, 3476) stores the K rows of one minibatch into the KV cache, once per layer and pass. save_k_impl (3351) is its body, which every worker of a shared window calls. store_k_block (3244) stores one run of consecutive tokens inside one block, whole or row by row.
One bit per page offset and storage slot, kept in the page, set when the K row at that offset is saved. note_k_row_saved sets one bit, and note_k_block_saved sets the 16 bits of a block at once.
The physical storage of one persistent K/V storage region (kv_storage_offset). A logical slot (kv_slot_id) maps to one under the active view.
Tokens per second, the decode throughput measure of the PR body's Performance section.

The lock on the scheduler's token tree. The scheduler thread (the thread that runs the scheduler of full.hpp between forward passes) holds it for clears (clear_kv_complete_at) and page copies (copy_from). No forward pass reads the book meanwhile.
The inference program under test. runtron is its command-line tool.
The CMake option that compiles the AMX kernels. The deb preset sets it on next to TRON_K_VNNI.

Vector Neural Network Instructions layout: the two values of one dimension pair of a token sit side by side, and one 64-byte row holds that pair for 16 consecutive tokens. It is the B-operand layout of the AMX tile multiply. VNNI-packed is the storage sense of packed.

The store of a run of 16 tokens that fills one block, written directly in the VNNI layout (PR #4898). This PR drops its mask parameter and makes the caller publish the block's bits with note_k_block_saved.

The shared K store of one minibatch (PR #4898). The main thread cuts the items into work units (runs inside one block of one page), opens the window, and the main helpers claim units. Every thread of the window, main included, claims units. Main then joins: it waits until every helper has finished, and only then records rows.

walkthrough.say: This is the last PR of the stack, and it fixes issue #4500: a generated token's K row written across 64 cache lines cost 2.2 % (tp2) and 9.7 % (tp4) of FPGA-attention decode throughput for qwen3-4b. The fix keeps an incomplete 16-token block row-major in its own bytes, converts it once at the forward end, and never converts the blocks that decode completes under hardware attention. Open the PR body's Short version and the stack table at the end of it.

Point at the two drawings of block 2: the same 4 KiB holds either four 256-byte rows per panel (the row-major form, row_major_row) or the 16 pair rows per panel (the VNNI form). Point at store_row_major / load_row_major, then at block_to_vnni and block_to_rows, and at the block bit k_vnni_blocks_ that says which form the block holds. Open h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:445-502 for the Note and the three row-major operations.

Point at the page column: k_rows_saved_ (one 64-bit word per state entry) and k_vnni_blocks_ (one byte per state entry), with one entry per logical slot plus the EAGLE entry. Point at k_state_ix and k_storage_ref: a logical slot maps to a state entry and a physical storage slot under the current view, and the pending list keeps the resolved pair. Open h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2613-2627 and 2139-2157.

Walk the states left to right: empty, incomplete (row-major), complete and waiting, converted. The 16th row sets the last row bit (note_k_row_saved, kv_cache.hpp:2169-2185), the forward end converts (k_block_to_vnni_at, 2216-2238), and the arc over the top is the whole-block save that goes straight to converted (note_k_block_saved, 2194-2202). Then point at the lower path: under hardware attention save_k records no bits, so the block never converts (model.hpp:3420-3425).

Follow the bytes of block 2: store_row_major writes 4 whole lines per token, block_to_vnni rewrites all 64 lines once at the forward end, store_row and load_row then touch 4 bytes in every one of the 64 lines for one token, and block_to_rows puts the row-major form back. Say the cost argument out loud: 4 lines per token in the row-major form against 64 in the VNNI form, for the store, the dotter and the FPGA staging gather. Open h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:503-533 for the two conversions and their 4 KiB stack copy.

Point at the run test: a run of 16 takes set_k_block and note_k_block_saved, any shorter run takes set_k_row per token (model.hpp:3303-3339), and set_k_row picks store_row_major or store_row from the block bit (kv_cache.hpp:2255-2260). Then point at the recording loop after the join (model.hpp:3419-3437): one note_k_row_saved per KV token, and a push onto pending_k_blocks_ when a row completes an unconverted block (one pending_k_block holds the page, its k_storage_ref and the block index, model.hpp:3167-3172, drawn in model-b1). The whole loop is skipped when cached_operation_uses_hw is true. Point at convert_pending_k_blocks at the bottom (3176-3183).

Point at the tinted band: the cooperative GOF staging gather of an earlier minibatch can still read a block's rows row-major while a later minibatch of the same pass saves the block's last rows. So the conversion waits until after wait_for_coop_gof. Open h/tron/models/model.hpp:1836-1847 to show run(), wait_for_coop_gof and convert_pending_k_blocks in that order. Then point at the token tree lane: clear_kv_complete_at and copy_from run between passes under the tree lock. So k_forget_row and copy_storage_slot need no bit synchronisation beyond it.

Use the rows as a checklist of every reader and writer: set_k_row / get_k_row branch on the block bit, k_row_if_row_major hands the FPGA staging a row-major row in place (full.hpp:2762-2764), k_forget_row drops bits and converts back (kv_cache.hpp:2557-2591), and copy_storage_slot carries the bits with the rows (2693-2789). Open h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:729-764 for the Note that states the policy and its accepted cost (a score can differ by fp32 add order alone, fp32 being the 32-bit float format of the score adds, when software scores such a block).
